newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-SAMPDORIA'S MIHAJLOVIC AND JUVE'S BOKSIC GET BANS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SAMPDORIA'S MIHAJLOVIC AND JUVE'S BOKSIC GET BANS.

text.p: Sampdoria's Yugoslav defender Sinisa Mihajlovic, picking up a four-match ban, led the list of suspensions in Italy's serie A on Wednesday while Croat stars Alen Boksic and Mario Stanic were also sidelined.
Juventus striker Boksic, who had just returned to the Italian league leaders from a lengthy injury, was suspended for two matches and Parma defender Stanic was banned for one game.
Mihajlovic was sent off on Sunday for aiming the ball at the referee after Atalanta were given a penalty.

The sporting judge said in his report that Mihajlovic had kicked the ball at the referee, without hitting him, and "uttered a disrespectful phrase at the referee, accompanied by gestures that repeated the content".
Boksic came on as a 77th-minute substitute in his first match since January and went off 10 minutes later for a foul in the 0-0 draw at Inter. It was his second red card of the season.
The judge said the Croat had hit Inter's Massimo Paganini in the face with his knee after bringing him down.
Inter's assistant coach Giacinto Facchetti was banned until March 24 for shouting abuse during the match.
Stanic, in his first season in Italian soccer, avoided expulsion in Parma's 2-1 win at Perugia but his booking brought him a suspension on accumulated points.
Other foreigners given one-match bans were Fiorentina's Swede Stefan Schwarz and Vicenza's Uruguayan Marcelo Otero.
